consumes: hash-bound generated exact-board testbench and declared instances SingleLayerSemanticHarness, ConnectedObservableLlamaStyleBlock, and spatialacc_exact_board_multilayer_tb
hierarchical_learning_context decision_policy and connected-kernel timing evidence
executable_actions.on_failure: Retain all active SACG contamination barriers and open retry requests; classify the result as a current board verification-capability blocker. Do not modify RTL, exact-wrapper sources, lifecycle predicates, testbench bindings, numeric policy, or immutable semantic inputs; do not rerun the completed connected-kernel replay or request unchanged-source VCS replay. Handoff the explicit unavailable-port report for approval-gated observer-contract reconciliation only if direct provenance remains incomplete.
executable_actions.rationale: Multi-agent system capability implementation is required for planned_tool.connected_kernel_boundary_signal_map. It must inspect only the hash-bound exact board source closure, declared testbench instances, and available elaboration metadata read-only to produce a complete direct mapping for all required current-DAG boundaries. This is the minimal current-layer action because the present trace cannot distinguish policy-legal pre-start core ingress from a stage0 transfer, while the certified connected kernel is closed evidence.

observations: The current board functional gate failed: all 16 tokens and 1792 ingress beats completed by cycle 20805737 while core egress was ready and accepted zero beats. This is a board-layer failure symptom, not a hardware pass or a proven RTL root cause.

The earliest CCTG records report core/stage0 ingress at cycle 20572946 before observed lifecycle start at cycle 20572948. That predicate conflicts with hierarchical_learning_context.decision_policy.accepted_input_handshake_required_before_kernel_lifecycle_start, so the current kernel_start-precedes-ingress findings cannot establish a block_input or kernel defect without direct signal provenance.

The existing exact-board testbench lacks declared direct valid, ready, payload, last, and accepted-count bindings for multiple required CCTG boundaries. In particular, it cannot lawfully produce direct first/last payload-digest evidence for the rms1 input and several residual, attention, and MLP paths without guessing ports.

The exact user-supplied board wrapper and selected simulation source closure are hash-bound and must remain unchanged. Current target-model expected output, checkpoint/stimulus provenance, complete validation-scope weight hashes, numeric policy, tolerance, semantic testbench meaning, token/tile/lane/word order, and Transformer-block-only golden scope are immutable.

The hash-validated connected-kernel evidence is closed: the certified replay has 1792 ingress and egress beats, terminal last-beat completion, 13-boundary liveness, and required elastic cross-token overlap. The current ambiguous observer trace does not directly contradict a named certified lower-layer invariant; no leaf or connected-kernel rerun is authorized.

sacg_memory_truth reports 24 active same-scope contamination barriers and 8 open same-scope retry requests, with no open same-scope backtrack request. These keep rejected artifacts as planning/debug evidence only and block promotion/downstream consumption, but do not prevent the bounded read-only current-layer provenance action.
proposed_actions: Perform only a read-only exact-board current-DAG boundary-signal provenance discovery. Map every required CCTG boundary to real elaborated valid, ready, payload, last, and accepted-count signals, or explicitly report it unavailable; do not guess names or create a surrogate wrapper.

Do not alter observer predicates, testbench instrumentation, RTL, wrapper sources, or functional artifacts in this action. Any later observer-only lifecycle reconciliation requires the resulting direct map and separate human approval.
Do not request an unchanged-source VCS replay, dependent board gates, backend tools, or connected-kernel replay before this capability result determines the next current-layer boundary action.
risks: Guessing hierarchical ports or deriving received counts/payloads from another boundary could falsely attribute a lifecycle, valid-ready, data-order, shape, numeric, memory-layout, runtime-loader, or AXI/DDR integration defect to the kernel.

Changing RTL, the exact wrapper, loader ABI, memory layout, pipeline architecture, tolerance, numeric policy, checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, or model scope to address an observer ambiguity would be unbounded and is not authorized.

The ready-egress/no-output symptom can still represent a real current-layer wrapper, harness, lifecycle, loader, ordering, AXI, DDR, or integration defect. It must remain a fail result until a direct source-hash-bound trace localizes it and later functional and semantic gates pass.

No board-level target-model numeric comparison, complete runtime-loader consumption proof, data-order pass, AXI protocol pass, DDR roundtrip pass, or output-count pass exists; none may be inferred from the lower-layer certificates or AXI heartbeat activity.
output.summary: Fail closed at board_axi_ddr_wrapped_system. The exact-board VCS run proves a ready-egress/zero-output semantic stall after 1792 accepted ingress beats, but the earliest lifecycle predicate is observationally inconsistent with the live policy requiring an accepted input handshake before kernel lifecycle start, and required direct current-DAG boundary port provenance is absent. The sole next causally distinct action is a read-only, hash-bound exact-board boundary-signal map. It must resolve whether the observed pre-start event is legal core ingress or a true stage0 transaction before any observer change, RTL/wrapper repair, or rerun. Certified operator-leaf and connected-kernel scopes remain closed; the completed connected-kernel targeted replay must not be rerun. Active same-scope SACG contamination barriers and open retry requests remain downstream-consumption and promotion blockers.
